text:
Mia: Heads up — CI microbench failure on PR #9428. bench/unit/kv_warmup shows ~8% tail-latency increase vs main. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/9428/artifacts

ci-bot: Test failed: bench/unit/kv_warmup (threshold 3%): delta = +8.1% (tails) — see artifacts

Raj: on it. quick skim of the artifact graphs looks like a different kernel/path is being picked for short seqs. could be the kernel-autoselect heuristic change from last week.

Oliver: which commit landed? I think the batching heuristics tweak (commit abc1234) and a small kernel-selector tweak (commit def5678) both merged in the same window.

Mia: PR includes def5678 (kernel selector) + quantization parity fixes. CI perf passed earlier but main has drift now. suspect selector first.

Sasha: I'll start a bisect on CI to isolate which merge introduced the regression. If bisect points to kernel selector, we'll try toggling the new heuristic flag.

Raj: repro locally with the same microbench harness:

```bash
./bench/runner --bench kv_warmup --model gpt-small --batching-window-ms 5 --sequence-dist short
```

Raj: I repro ~7% tail increase locally when I enable the new selector heuristic. pprof shows more time in memcpy and kernel boundary overhead.

Oliver: interesting — memcpy spike suggests we're falling back to an unfused kernel for short sequences. maybe the selector prefers a quantized path that changes memory layout.

Mia: can you paste the perf flame?

Raj: attaching snippet:

```
# top samples
memcpy 32.4%
kv_dispatcher::choose_kernel 18.1%
kernel_x::execute 12.2%
```

Raj: compare to main where memcpy is ~10%. big jump.

Sasha: CI bisect update: candidate commit def5678 (kernel-autoselect v2) is the first that reproduces on CI. bisect results: def5678 -> +8.3%, abc1234 -> no repro.

Mia: okay flag that PR as rollout blocker. If we can toggle the flag to revert behavior without full revert that's preferable.

Oliver: created a quick feature-flag toggle: `runtime.kernel_autoselect_v2 = false`. Patch applied to the PR branch and rerunning microbench on CI.

ci-bot: Rerun started for bench/unit/kv_warmup on PR #9428 (with runtime.kernel_autoselect_v2=false).

Henry: if the toggle fixes it, we should ship a revert for the selector commit in the release branch and follow up with a proper fix. Avoid rolling back batching heuristics since they didn't repro.

Raj: re-run results: with flag off, delta = +0.6% (within noise). pprof shows memcpy back to ~11%.

Mia: great. mark the PR as temporary-blocked and add note "kernel_autoselect_v2 causes kv warmup tail regression; toggle disabled pending fix".

Sasha: I'll open a revert PR against main for def5678 and also a tracking issue to reintroduce once we adjust kernel scoring to prefer fused paths for short seqs.

Oliver: created revert PR #9435: https://git.internal/redwood/revert-def5678. Also adding a unit test that asserts the kernel selection for sequence-length < 64 picks fused_kernel when mem footprint small.

Henry: let's add an alert to our perf dashboard to catch this class of regression earlier: add a check for kv_warmup tail > 3% after PR merges (run microbench with short-seq profile).

Mia: thanks team. Actions: Sasha opens revert + issue, Oliver adds unit test and feature-flag guard, Raj writes perf investigation notes with pprof and flamegraphs, Henry updates dashboard. I'll follow up in the release channel once revert lands. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Revert PR #9435 created and CI started.

Sasha: filing tracking issue: https://issues.internal/redwood/INF-1287 — kernel_autoselect_v2 causes fused-kernel regression for short sequences; follow-ups: scoring fix, more unit tests, and perf gating on merges.

Mia: leaving this thread here for audit. If anyone re-enables v2, ping #eng-runtime and set a gated rollout.

Oliver: note for postmortem — include test case and exact perf numbers (before/after) and the bisect timeline.

Henry: copy that. I'll draft the postmortem once revert is merged.

Sasha: revert passed CI and merged to main at 2481124500. closing bisect.

Mia: thanks all.
